vid_urls.title: SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches U.S. Space Force satellites from Vandenberg, California
vid_urls.description:
Watch live coverage as SpaceX launches a Falcon 9 rocket from California carrying a classified payload for the U.S. Space Force. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base is scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 28, during a window that opens at 8:39 p.m. PST / 11:39 p.m. EDT (0439 UTC on Sunday).

The first-stage booster, serial number B1082, launching for an 27th time, will land on the drone ship 'Of Course I Still Love You' about 8.5 minutes into the flight.

The USSF-380 mission will take a south-easterly trajectory upon departure from Vandenberg. 

Live commentary from Spaceflight Now's Will Robinson-Smith will be provided starting about 30 minutes prior to launch.

vid_urls.title: NASA's Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 Launch
vid_urls.description:
We're bringing the holidays to the International Space Station!

NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 10:47 a.m. EST (1547 UTC), Sunday, Nov. 29, for the next launch delivering science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the orbiting laboratory. 

Northrop Grumman's Cygnus XL spacecraft, lifting off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, will also carry fresh fruit, holiday cookies, and kits for making pizza, tacos and gingerbread houses.

The uncrewed Cygnus XL is scheduled to dock with the station on Tuesday, Dec. 1. Learn more about the timeline and the mission: https://go.nasa.gov/4eI0RBH
